### tapectl report needs

Each unit's copy target, copies and shortfall at every location

A unit's targets are its resolved `copies_at` map (an archive set's `required_locations` counts as one copy at each name), raised by the tape-only multiplier for a tape-only unit, and its copy floor is the larger of `min_copies` and the map's sum. Lists the units that have a target or are short of their copy floor; `--all` lists every unit.

With `--location`, only that location, and each unit's need there: group 1 when its target there is unmet, group 2 when it is short of its copy floor with no target there and no copy there yet.

```text
tapectl report needs [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**

- `--location <LOCATION>` — Only this location, with each unit's need there
- `--all` — Every unit, not only those with a target or a copy shortfall

### tapectl report compaction-candidates

Volumes flagged for compaction

With `--plan`, also groups the flagged volumes whose live data fits one destination tape, largest reclaim first, and says how to compact each group (`volume rewrite` for one volume, in place; `--with-staged` to carry the others onto its cartridge).

```text
tapectl report compaction-candidates [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**

- `--plan` — Group the candidates by what fits one destination tape
- `--generation <GENERATION>` — Plan for destination tapes of this generation (e.g. LTO-6, LTO-7) instead of the drive's own. Only with --plan

### tapectl report failed-stages

Stage attempts that failed, and the hours each lost

Every `stage create` that ended without staging its unit, from the facts the catalog keeps: when it started, the last moment it recorded (its phases, dar's report, its source check), and the hours between, with the total. A failed stage restarts its unit from the beginning (ADR-0012 item 91), so this is the time it cost.

```text
tapectl report failed-stages [OPTIONS]
```
